summary: Redwood AE and SE ran a POC scoping call with Acme Health to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timelines for a security-focused pilot. Key compliance questions centered on SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML configuration, RBAC scopes, audit-log retention and KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send compliance docs and benchmark plan; Acme to provide datasets, network constraints, and infra contacts; schedule private deployment demo in two weeks.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Ana Rivera (Acme Health), Tom Brooks (Acme - Security), Priya Singh (Acme - Cloud Ops), Elliot Moore (Acme PM)

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, uh, really excited to run through the POC scoping for the security pilot. Quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Ana Rivera: Hi all, Ana here, head of data science at Acme. We're focused on extracting structured data from clinical notes and want to make sure PHI handling and compliance are rock solid.
[00:23] Tom Brooks: Tom, security architect. I'll be driving the compliance checklist and infra approvals.
[00:29] Priya Singh: Priya, cloud ops, I'll be our infra contact for networking and deployment.
[00:34] Elliot Moore: Elliot, PM, I'll coordinate timelines.
[00:37] Laura Chen: Great; Marcus, want to intro?
[00:40] Marcus Patel: Yeah hey all, Marcus Patel, SE on the inference team. I'll lead benchmarking and the private deployment demo if needed.
[00:46] Laura Chen: Cool. Agenda: success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks, timelines, and then deep dive on security/compliance requirements — SOC 2/ISO, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS.

[02:05] Laura Chen: To kick off, how are you thinking about success — is it latency, cost, throughput, or data residency?
[02:12] Elliot Moore: Primary success is non-functional: under 200ms 95th percentile for our clinical extraction flows and end-to-end throughput to support peak batch of ~500 concurrent inference requests. Then of course auditability and no PHI leakage.
[02:27] Dr. Ana Rivera: Also quality: F1 on entity extraction should be within 3 points of our baseline model.

[03:05] Marcus Patel: Good — so we're hearing latency target ~200ms p95, concurrency ~500, and quality delta <=3pts. We'll map that to model variant and batching. For dedicated vs hosted, any preference?
[03:20] Tom Brooks: Security trumps cost for the pilot. We want a private deployment or dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS if possible.
[03:31] Priya Singh: We need the control plane to not hold unredacted PHI; ideally data never leaves our VPC during inference.

[04:15] Laura Chen: Noted. For SOC 2/ISO, do you need evidence of Redwood's reports or also evidence of the private deployment's configuration?
[04:24] Tom Brooks: Both. We'll need Redwood's SOC 2 report and ISO scope to start. For the pilot we also need a runbook that documents how audit logs are captured, where KMS keys live, and RBAC mappings.
[04:38] Marcus Patel: We'll share SOC 2 and ISO summary. For private deployments we can provide a deployment checklist detailing KMS integration options — HSM vs cloud KMS — and how audit logs are forwarded.

[05:45] Dr. Ana Rivera: On SSO, we use Okta and want SAML 2.0 based SSO for console access and SCIM for user provisioning. Can Redwood support SCIM and SAML?
[05:55] Laura Chen: Yes, we support SAML and SCIM. For private deployments there's an SSO connector we ship; we'll include SAML metadata and our IdP setup guide.

[06:21] Tom Brooks: RBAC — we need role separation: read-only analysts vs deploy/ops vs security auditors. Do you have granular roles?
[06:29] Marcus Patel: We expose RBAC with role templates; can map custom roles. We'll send a sample RBAC matrix to review.

[07:10] Priya Singh: Audit logs: retention is key. Our policy is 7 years for some audit trails, at least 1 year for others. Can Redwood support configurable retention and export to our SIEM?
[07:23] Laura Chen: We can forward logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export; retention is configurable on private deployments. For hosted API there are retention defaults — but for enterprise pilots we have extended retention options.

[08:05] Marcus Patel: Regarding KMS, do you prefer customer-managed keys in your cloud KMS or an on-prem HSM?
[08:12] Tom Brooks: Prefer customer-managed KMS in our cloud (AWS KMS) first; HSM is a possibility later.

[09:00] Laura Chen: Let's talk benchmarks: Marcus, what do you need from Acme to size the workload?
[09:06] Marcus Patel: Sample prompts, average and max token lengths, expected QPS (baseline and peak), and payload sizes. Also whether requests are streaming or full-response.
[09:18] Dr. Ana Rivera: We'll provide representative prompt set (~200 prompts) and profile of batch jobs — mostly synchronous requests, occasional heavy batch of 10k items overnight.

[10:02] Marcus Patel: For the concurrency of ~500, we need to simulate that concurrency with a synthetic load; we'll define a run that hits model variants and measures p95 latency and token throughput. Also will test prefix caching efficacy for repeated prefixes.

[11:00] Elliot Moore: Timeline — we'd like pilot kickoff in the week of 2025-08-19 and run 3 weeks of evaluation. Is that feasible?
[11:10] Laura Chen: Yes, if we can get docs and network details this week, Redwood can prepare the private tenant and benchmark harness.

[12:30] Tom Brooks: On legal: any data processing addendum (DPA) and terms? We'll need DPA and if possible a draft for review.
[12:40] Laura Chen: We'll share our standard DPA and can discuss any required addenda.

[13:25] Elliot Moore: For success criteria recap: performance (p95 <200ms), throughput (support 500 concurrent), quality (F1 within 3 pts), and compliance checks (SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SAML, RBAC, audit logs).
[13:40] Marcus Patel: I'll convert that into acceptance tests in the benchmark plan.

[14:10] Dr. Ana Rivera: A note on dataset: some of the records are de-identified, some are limited PHI. We need strict logging and no retention beyond agreed windows. Also, is there any model telemetry that could leak PHI?
[14:24] Marcus Patel: We'll ensure request/response logging scrubs sensitive fields by default in the private deployment, and we can provide the telemetry schema. Also recommend tokenization checks for PI-like patterns.

[15:20] Tom Brooks: On networking: Priya, do you have constraints?
[15:24] Priya Singh: We'll require VPC peering with static routes, limited inbound IPs, and mutual TLS for control-plane traffic. Also NAT restrictions for egress — only to allowed endpoints.
[15:36] Laura Chen: We can accommodate VPC peering and mTLS; Marcus will include network checklist.

[16:50] Marcus Patel: Benchmarks specifics: we'll run three phases — baseline latency tests, throughput/concurrency ramp, and quality/regression tests against your labeled set. We'll instrument token-level latency and cost-per-token.

[17:30] Dr. Ana Rivera: For quality tests, we'll provide a 500-example gold set and evaluation script.

[18:10] Elliot Moore: Are there any red flags around support or SLA for pilot?
[18:16] Laura Chen: For Dedicated/private pilots we offer priority support and a 99.9% uptime objective for the serving runtime; for production we can discuss formal SLAs.

[19:05] Tom Brooks: We want to verify that audit logs include user identity, action, timestamp, request/response IDs, and a checksum.
[19:16] Marcus Patel: Yes we capture user identity, role, action, resource, timestamp, request_id; for response data we can log metadata only unless you opt-in for full response logs with tighter controls.

[20:30] Priya Singh: Encryption in transit and at rest — do you support TLS 1.2/1.3 and AES-256?
[20:36] Laura Chen: Yes, TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-flight, AES-256 for at-rest. For private deployments you can bring your CMK.

[22:00] Tom Brooks: Any third-party dependencies in the control plane that might affect compliance?
[22:07] Marcus Patel: Our control plane uses several managed services; we'll provide a list and a security posture summary for each.

[23:15] Laura Chen: I'll send SOC 2 and ISO summary, SAML/SCIM guide, RBAC sample matrix, and the DPA today or by 2025-08-09. Marcus will draft the benchmark plan and runbook by 2025-08-12.

[24:00] Tom Brooks: For the bench tests, can we do an initial smoke run in a staging private tenant before full load?
[24:10] Marcus Patel: Absolutely — smoke then ramp. We'll include the smoke checklist.

[25:40] Elliot Moore: On timelines again — if we get artifacts this week, kickoff 8/19, run 3-week pilot, decision meeting first week of September?
[25:52] Laura Chen: That timeline sounds right.

[27:00] Dr. Ana Rivera: A quick question on model variants — do you recommend quantized models for cost savings or full fp16 for best quality?
[27:08] Marcus Patel: We'll test both. For extraction tasks quantized int8 often matches quality while saving cost — but we'll validate on your gold set.

[28:20] Priya Singh: Any special onboarding for our infra team?
[28:25] Laura Chen: We'll run a private deployment onboarding session with infra and security — include runbooks, network diagram, SAML setup, KMS onboarding.

[30:00] Tom Brooks: About audit log export: can logs be pushed to our Splunk or S3 with server-side encryption using our CMK?
[30:09] Marcus Patel: Yes to both; S3 exports can be encrypted with your CMK and we can push to Splunk via secure forwarder.

[31:50] Elliot Moore: Any blockers we should surface now?
[31:54] Tom Brooks: None besides getting SOC 2/ISO and DPA reviewed quickly.

[33:10] Laura Chen: We'll attach the SOC 2 and ISO documents and a short CSV of the control mappings to your security contact.

[34:20] Dr. Ana Rivera: On data residency: some of our data must remain in us-east-1; any objections?
[34:28] Laura Chen: We can pin region to us-east-1 for the private tenant.

[35:15] Marcus Patel: I'll also include the benchmark harness repo link and a sample load script.

[36:05] Priya Singh: For SAML metadata exchange, we'll need ACS and entityID placeholders — please provide your SP metadata.

[36:22] Laura Chen: We'll provide SP metadata in the SAML guide.

[37:45] Elliot Moore: Let's confirm acceptance criteria rundown for the pilot doc.

[37:51] Marcus Patel: I'll author acceptance tests: p95 latency, concurrency sustained for 2 hours at target load, quality thresholds on gold set, successful SSO login and RBAC enforcement, audit-log exports validated.

[39:00] Tom Brooks: Ok, and contact for legal/contract?

[39:04] Laura Chen: I'll introduce you to our legal rep in the follow-up email.

[40:10] Dr. Ana Rivera: Anything about model weights handling — do you retain model versions or logs that could be considered derived sensitive data?

[40:20] Marcus Patel: Model weights are managed by Redwood runtime; for private deployment the runtime is deployed into your infra and logs are under your control. We can enable minimal telemetry.

[41:30] Priya Singh: CI/CD hooks — will we have a way to pin model versions and roll back?

[41:35] Marcus Patel: Yes, we support version pinning and can do canary rollouts; we'll document rollout APIs.

[43:10] Elliot Moore: Any final questions?

[43:15] Tom Brooks: No further questions.

[43:18] Dr. Ana Rivera: None from my side.

[43:22] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone. Recap of next steps and I'll follow up with attachments.

[44:00] Laura Chen: Meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors and simplified speaker labels.
